# Support agent escalation

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-003**: A `switch` over `EscalationTrigger` with no `default` MUST compile, so a member added without a matching case fails `npm run typecheck`; each PR that adds a member updates the exhaustive-switch fixture in the same PR, so `npm run typecheck` proves the member was handled everywhere, not skipped. As built, the fixture is `apps/api/test/fixtures/escalationTriggers.ts`, typechecked since #275: a `Record` over `EscalationTrigger` rather than a `switch`, because a member added without an entry fails `npm run typecheck` the same way, and a switch over every member exceeds the lint complexity limit. Validated by `npm run typecheck` over its `satisfies` clause. (#24, #151, #178)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `EscalationTrigger` is a union of `tms_unavailable`, `tms_timeout`, `no_tool_for_question`, `customer_asked_for_human`, `out_of_scope_change_request`; a `switch` over it with no `default` compiles, failing `npm run typecheck` if a trigger is added without a matching case elsewhere
- [ ] A tool call returning `unavailable` or `timeout` marks an escalation with no model action - tested with a mock provider emitting no `escalate_to_human` call, asserting one record exists
- [ ] A `not_found` from the same fixture marks no escalation
- [ ] `escalate_to_human` is registered, declares exactly one required enum-constrained `reason_category`; a call with an invalid value is rejected by `037`'s validation as a readable tool result, not a throw, with a `stream_end`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `EscalationTrigger` has exactly six members with `model_call_failed` added, and the existing no-`default` exhaustive-switch fixture compiles again in the same PR - `npm run typecheck` proves the sixth member was handled everywhere, not skipped
- [ ] A turn on the real engine whose provider rejects with an `AIError` produces exactly one escalation document with `model_call_failed` in its triggers, zero TMS transport calls, and no `escalate_to_human` call from the mock provider - the trigger is code-fired, not model-fired
- [ ] The same test asserts the caller still receives the `AIError` - recording the escalation does not swallow the failure, so the existing customer-facing notice path is unchanged

## Why

The escalation path today has exactly two triggers: a TMS tool result marked unavailable or timeout, and the model itself calling the escalate-to-human tool. A provider failure fires neither - it throws before any tool round even runs, so there's no tool result to map and no model left to call anything. A prior fix shipped only the customer-facing half of this gap: the customer reads a Danish error notice, but no row reaches the escalation collection and nobody at OLT learns the conversation ended.
